newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina House approves $11.4 billion budget.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina House approves $11.4 billion budget.

text.p: North Carolina's House of Representatives tentatively approved a $11.4 billion budget after rejecting a proposal to cap state spending.
The budget, which raises overall spending by about 7.0 percent, was approved on a first reading Wednesday. It was awaiting a second vote Thursday, and then would go to the Senate for negotiations.

The House plan would raise salaries by about 6.5 percent for teachers and 4.0 percent for other state workers. It allocates $21.9 million to expand the Smart Start prgram for preschoolers and cuts the state sales tax on food to two percent from three percent.

In an 83-36 vote Wednesday, the House rejected a proposal by Rep. Chuck Neely, R-Raleigh, to cap state spending growth at 6.0 percent a year and prohibit spending from rising faster than personal income.
